title: Reduce span noise and introduce observability fast-path
creator: Carlos Mendes
description:
Background: The runtime continues to emit a high volume of low-value tracing spans and high-cardinality fields from hot request paths. This increases allocation pressure, raises ingestion costs, and complicates downstream analysis. Recent instrument upgrades (OpenTelemetry SDK bump) revealed several hotpaths where span creation and context propagation are avoidable or can be deferred.

Goal: Implement a fast-path for hot RPC/handler code that avoids span allocation and metadata enrichment for non-error, short-lived requests while preserving full traces for sampled/error flows. Reduce metric and log cardinality by normalizing a handful of noisy attributes. Deliver measurable CPU and memory allocation improvements and a >30% reduction in trace events per second for baseline traffic.

Scope:
- Add a lightweight trace fast-path (no allocation) enabled by a sampling predicate and feature flag.
- Introduce a per-process normalized attribute map with allowed keys and value scrubbers for logs/metrics.
- Replace a few expensive enrichment hooks with async, bounded worker pipelines where needed (non-blocking).
- Add e2e benchmarks and CI gating to assert negative regressions.

Out of scope: model-level instrumentation changes, third-party SDK rewrites, long-term storage retention policy changes.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmark shows >= 30% reduction in emitted spans/tick for our p50 traffic profile
No increase in p95 latency greater than 5ms for the instrumented endpoints
Span allocation per-request reduced (measured via runtimetools) by >= 40% on average
Feature flag to toggle fast-path is behind runtime config and defaults to off
Unit and integration tests added for sampling predicate, attribute scrubbers, and fallback path
Code reviewed and merged; rollout plan and monitoring dashboard published
tasks: Audit hot callsites that allocate spans (instrumentation grep + flamegraph)
Design fast-path interface: TraceContext.tryFastSpan() with no allocations
Implement sampling predicate that can be evaluated before allocation
Add attribute normalization/scrubbing table with allowlist and reducers
Add metric/log instrumentation changes to reference normalized attributes
Implement async enrichment worker for expensive lookups with bounded queue
Add load and allocation benchmarks (locally and on perf infra)
Add feature flag, config, and rollout plan (1% -> 25% -> 100%)
Create dashboard widgets: span rate, allocation delta, route latency
Write migration notes for SDK consumers and internal docs
notes: Decision: prefer no-allocation fast-path over object pooling to avoid GC churn
Tradeoff: some low-importance traces will be lossy under fast-path; we'll keep full traces for errors and sampled sessions
We aligned on a small allowlist of attributes: route, shard, region. All others will be hashed/truncated
We will gate fast-path behind a runtime flag and rollout by service to monitor regressions
Follow-up: evaluate moving non-critical enrichment to pre-warmed background worker across services
